known_issues.label: General Fund expense
known_issues.note: The General Fund expense lines for 2025 add to $186,157,601, $7 more than the printed Grand Total of $186,157,594; for 2026 they add to $201,945,911, $11 more than the printed $201,945,900. Each department's lines are within $3 of its printed total (pp. 12-28), and the printed department totals add to the Grand Total within $2, so the gap is the book's own rounding spread over 14-18 departments. Under the printed-totals rule this is rounding only (the allowance for a roll-up of about 1,200 lines is $0.50 a line), so the site shows the printed Grand Total with no flag. Lines are shown as printed.

known_issues.label: General Fund expense
known_issues.note: The 2023 General Fund expense lines in the 2024 book add to $178,358,141, $6 less than the printed Grand Total of $178,358,147 (p120). The printed department totals add to the Grand Total within $5 (the extractor's check), so the gap is the book's own rounding spread over about 1,200 lines. Under the printed-totals rule this is rounding only (allowance $0.50 a line for a roll-up), so the site shows the printed Grand Total with no flag. Lines are shown as printed.

known_issues.label: Fund B Excess (deficiency) of revenues over (under) expenditures
known_issues.note: Liquid Fuels schedule: the variance printed for Excess and for Net change subtracts the expenditure variance from the revenue variance (total revenues variance minus total expenditures variance) instead of adding it. Every other schedule, and every other row of this one, prints the favourable difference from the final budget (actual - final for revenue and the net lines; final - actual for expenditure), and adding the two gives Actual - Final. The same error is in all three ACFRs (2023 p126, 2024 p124, 2025 p122). The Original, Final and Actual columns foot; only the printed variance is wrong. The site does not show printed variances.

known_issues.label: 2023 General Fund original expenditure + transfers out vs County-2024-Budget-Book.pdf
known_issues.note: The ACFR's 2023 'Original' General Fund budget is total expenditures 172,362,634 plus transfers out 13,758,442 = 186,121,076; the 2024 book's 2023 column (and Resolution 109 of 2022, 178,358,147) gives 178,358,141. Original revenue ties (178,585,614 vs 178,585,615) and the County match (transfers out 13,758,442) ties, so the 7.76M gap is in operating spending. It is close to the 7,948,024 of 2022 encumbrances carried into 2023 in Res 109 (185,095 apart), but the ACFR does not say what its Original column includes; cause not confirmed. Debt service also differs: ACFR principal + interest 21,700,878 vs Res 109 21,423,128. The site uses the book for the 2023 budget and the ACFR only for the actual, and computes no variance from this Original column (docs/COUNTY_RESEARCH.md, ACFR import spec section 4).

known_issues.label: 2024 General Fund original expenditure + transfers out vs County-2025-Budget-Book.pdf
known_issues.note: The ACFR's 2024 'Original' General Fund budget is total expenditures 185,071,157 plus transfers out 13,794,916 = 198,866,073, against the 2025 book's 2024 column 182,561,646 (Resolution 91 of 2023: 182,561,641). Revenue ties (182,661,641), and book accounts 7965 transfers (13,794,916), 7953 principal (14,145,000) and 7951 interest (5,357,776) equal the ACFR's lines, so the 16.3M gap is in current spending: the ACFR's Original prints capital outlay 7,989,713 where the book has 572,010. The ACFR's original net change is (16,204,432); the adopted resolution balances with +100,000. Part may be the 6,376,194 of 2023 encumbrances carried into 2024 (Res 91), which leaves about 9.9M unexplained; the MD&A (p35) says only that the budget was later increased for ARPA and ERAP. Cause not found. The site uses the book for the 2024 budget and computes no variance from this Original column.

known_issues.label: 2024 General Fund Transfers out actual vs governmental funds statement p43
known_issues.note: The 2024 General Fund budget-vs-actual schedule (County-ACFR-2024.pdf p114) prints Transfers out actual (18,962,872), which repeats to the dollar the 2023 figure (County-ACFR-2023.pdf p116, and the 2023 governmental funds statement p43). The County's 2024 governmental funds statement (County-ACFR-2024.pdf p43) prints General Fund transfers out of (21,630,095), which equals total transfers in to the other funds (22,249,247) less the Block Grant fund's own transfer out (619,152). Transfers are on the same basis in both statements (in 2023 and 2025 the two figures are equal). The schedule's below-the-line 'Net decrease in due from other funds' (8,075,584) also repeats a 2023 figure. The schedule's net change (3,003,261) foots with 18,962,872. The site shows 18,962,872 as printed on p114, flagged with this note.

known_issues.label: 2024 General Fund Net change in fund balances
known_issues.note: The schedule's 2024 General Fund net change (3,003,261, p114) is computed with Transfers out of (18,962,872), which repeats the 2023 figure (see the Transfers out entry for p114). With the governmental funds statement's (21,630,095) on p43 the net change would be 336,038. The site shows the printed figure with this flag.

known_issues.label: 2025 Fund Y original expenditure vs County-2026-Budget-Book.pdf
known_issues.note: Children and Youth Services 2025: the ACFR's 'original' (and final) expenditure is 53,335,444, the same total to the dollar as its 2024 original (2024 ACFR p115), while the 2025 and 2026 books give 57,657,397 for fund Y. The ACFR's 2025 original revenue plus transfers in (44,816,706 + 12,840,687 = 57,657,393) does equal the book, and the schedule therefore prints an original net change of +4,321,949. The expenditure budget looks carried forward from 2024 in the ACFR. The site shows the book's budget and the ACFR's actual only, not the ACFR's original.

known_issues.label: Fund Balance Available 12/31/24
known_issues.note: Resolution No. 83 of 2024 (the 2025 budget) prints $69,155,866 as the General Fund's "Fund Balance Available 12/31/24". That is exactly the audited General Fund balance at 12/31/2023 in the 2023 audited report (statistical Table 3). The audited balance at 12/31/2024 is $74,186,759 (2024 audited report, Table 3). The resolution's footnote says the figure includes $550,000 in prior fiscal year cost saving measures. The same figure and label are reprinted in the 2025 budget book. The resolution's balances are budget figures, not audited ones, so the site shows $69,155,866 as printed, as the 2025 Budget's opening balance, and shows the audited balances separately as Actual.

actuals_note: Actual figures come from the County's audited Annual Comprehensive Financial Report. They are reported by fund, revenue source and function, not by department or account line, so they appear next to budget totals and not next to line items.

Actuals are on the County's budgetary (cash-like) basis, and include grant revenue and spending added after the budget was adopted (ARPA, ERAP, opioid funds). Actual revenue ran 10-15% above the adopted budget in 2023-2025, largely for that reason. Compare actual with the final budget in the ACFR, not only with the adopted budget.
Behavioral Health, Developmental Services (Intellectual Disabilities) and Early Intervention are reported together.
2026 has no actuals yet: the 2026 ACFR will be published around mid-2027.

The budget books count transfers to other funds (the County match) as General Fund expenditure, and count them again as revenue of the receiving special funds. The ACFR reports transfers separately from revenue and expenditure, so compare a book's total with the actual total plus transfers.
The budget shown is the County's adopted budget from its budget books. The ACFR's own 'original budget' column is not used: for 2023 and 2024 it does not match the adopted budget.
